article.title: NFL EDGE Tuesday Evening Brief
article.dek: Caleb Williams is trending toward a Sunday return, the Ravens wait on Lamar, and Thursday's total is drifting down ahead of kickoff.

items.headline: Caleb Williams trending toward a Sunday return
paragraphs: The biggest quarterback story of the day is in Chicago. Ian Rapoport reported Monday that all signs point to Caleb Williams being back on the field this week for the Bears' trip to Atlanta. Head coach Ben Johnson called Williams 'on track' — then hedged, adding he thinks it's going to be close.
The market heard the optimistic part. Chicago flipped from a 1.5-point underdog at open to a 3-point favorite, now -120 to cover the spread. That's a 4.5-point swing on one quarterback's hamstring.

One honest flag: the app's quarterback feed still lists Tyson Bagent as Chicago's expected starter. The optimism hasn't reached the board yet. Until it does, the app is pricing a different game — which is exactly when you run Check with your book's line instead of trusting a stale number.
items.takeaway: Williams is trending yes, not official yet — bet the practice reports, not the rumor.

SI Betting: Bears flip to -3 favorites on Williams optimism

items.headline: Two more QB watches: Penix and Lamar
paragraphs: Michael Penix Jr.'s rib injury is not considered serious, per Adam Schefter. He might play Sunday against the Bears, but Atlanta wants to see him practice this week before deciding. If he can't go, it's Tua Tagovailoa again.
Lamar Jackson is 'definitely doing better,' per head coach Jesse Minter — but Minter couldn't guarantee anything for Sunday in Cleveland, not even Wednesday practice. Still no official word.

The app feed still shows Tyler Huntley as Baltimore's expected starter. Same deal as Chicago: the board is pricing the backup until the starter is official. Watch Wednesday and Thursday practice participation — that's the real signal. Final inactive lists land about 90 minutes before kickoff.
items.takeaway: Penix a maybe, Lamar still a mystery — the app hasn't flipped on either.

items.headline: Thursday: Seahawks at Broncos kicks off Week 6
paragraphs: Seattle visits Denver on Thursday night — 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff at Empower Field at Mile High, on Prime Video. The Seahawks are 2.5-point favorites at DraftKings (-118), with Denver +2.5 (-102).

Denver weather Thursday: morning rain, then clearing by evening. Low around 34 degrees, wind out of the southwest near 8 mph at kickoff time. That's the forecast, plain and simple — not an edge, just the conditions.
Thursday game? Thursday check. The Week 6 card lands when the board flips, and this is the first game on it.
items.takeaway: Week 6 starts Thursday in Denver. Thursday game? Thursday check.

items.headline: Both Week 5 cards cashed — here's the read
paragraphs: The Hit Rate card was on Buffalo's moneyline at +154. The app's model gave the Bills a 57.3% chance against the market's 37.5%. The underdog won outright in overtime. That's what the Hit Rate lane is for — it chases the win, not the value. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate, and that's not a knock. Last night it did exactly its job.
The Balanced card took Buffalo +3.5 at -115, the middle ground: a strong pick without paying too much. The model had it at 50.5% against the market's 48.6%. It cashed with room to spare.
The Value lane sat the week out — no offer met its contract. Some weeks the disciplined move is no move at all.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate chased the win and found it; Balanced took the points and covered.

items.headline: The Week 6 card isn't on the board yet — here's the plan
paragraphs: The app refreshed this evening and it's still showing Week 5. The Week 6 slate — Thursday night first — lands when the board flips, and the card re-runs on the new numbers then.

Until then, don't bet Monday's numbers blind. And if your book isn't showing DK or FD prices, that's what Check is for: type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet-or-no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
The board refreshes every morning and evening. When it flips to Week 6, the Thursday card will be waiting.
items.takeaway: Report the news first, then use it: the Week 6 card lands on the flip — Check makes it your number.

items.headline: Learn the Game: steam move
paragraphs: Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: imagine a team's line opens at -3 on Monday morning. By Thursday it's -5, and there's been no injury news at all. Bettors call that a steam move — the market sprinting one direction on heavy, respected action.

Why it matters: steam usually means sharp money hit the same side at multiple books, fast. But here's the catch — the price you get after the steam is not the price the steam got. Chasing a move after it's already run is paying retail for someone else's wholesale ticket.

Our Fade rule needs a verified tickets-vs-handle split plus corroboration before it becomes a real play. I checked the free splits row tonight: tickets and handle were on the same side in every market, so no split qualified — the classroom stays open.
items.takeaway: Steam tells you where the money went, not where the value is — the number you can actually bet is the only one that matters.

items.headline: Bears swing 4.5 points on Williams optimism
paragraphs: This is the move of the day. Chicago opened as a 1.5-point underdog at Atlanta and is now a 3-point favorite, -120 to cover. The entire swing is Caleb Williams optimism — Rapoport's 'all signs point' report plus Johnson's 'on track.'

The app hasn't caught it: the board is still Week 5 and the quarterback feed still shows Bagent. If you like Chicago at the new number, run it through Check with your book's actual line and price — the app re-evaluates at your number, not Monday's.
items.takeaway: A 4.5-point quarterback swing the app hasn't priced yet. Shop the number you can actually bet.

items.headline: Thursday total drifting down
paragraphs: Seahawks-Broncos opened 42.5 and the total is sliding — 41.5 at some books now. The spread is steadier: Seattle -2.5 (-118 at DraftKings), with -3 available elsewhere. Denver's Thursday forecast shows morning rain clearing by evening, low in the mid-30s.
When the board flips to Week 6, the app prices the Thursday game at whatever the lines are then — not where they opened. That's the number that counts.
items.takeaway: Total sliding, spread steady. The flip prices the current number, not the opener.

items.headline: Ravens holding -4.5
paragraphs: Baltimore moved from -3.5 to -4.5 on Monday's Lamar optimism and it's holding there at -110. But the optimism is still just optimism — Minter wouldn't confirm anything for Sunday, and the app still prices the game with Huntley.
If Lamar is confirmed, that number won't sit still. If he's out, -4.5 with Huntley off an overtime road win is a different conversation. Either way, Check re-runs it at your price.
items.takeaway: Holding -4.5 on hope, not confirmation. News moves this one next.

items.headline: Thursday game? Thursday check.
paragraphs: The Week 6 card isn't on the board yet, so tonight's move is preparation, not action. When the board flips, open the Thursday game, and if your book's line differs from what the app shows, type yours into Check. The app runs your price back through the model and the evaluator and hands you a bet-or-no-bet verdict on the number you can actually get.
And the occasional honest nudge: settlement is manual — the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself. Log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Prep tonight, decide Thursday — and keep the tracker honest.
